summary: Updates RFC 3777 to allow the announcement of open positions and the request for volunteers for the nominating committee before its chair is named by the Internet Society President. It is a Best Current Practice, replaced by RFC 7437.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5633 lets the IETF Executive Director start announcing open positions and collecting NomCom volunteers before the incoming chair is named. The chair search and volunteer solicitation can then happen at the same time; RFC 7437 later obsoleted this update.

questions: how does the ietf pick leaders
who volunteers for the nominating committee
when can the ietf executive director solicit nomcom volunteers
subtitle: Allow the IETF to request NomCom volunteers before its chair is named.

tldr.problem: The NomCom volunteer solicitation could not begin until its chair was named, so a delay in naming the chair also delayed the committee's work.
tldr.mechanism: If no chair is named four weeks after the first IETF meeting of the year, the IETF Executive Director can announce open positions and solicit volunteers on the incoming chair's behalf.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5633 updates RFC 3777 and was obsoleted by RFC 7437.

facts.label: Deadline to start early solicitation
facts.value: Four weeks after the first IETF meeting

today: RFC 5633 is a Best Current Practice, updates RFC 3777, and was obsoleted by RFC 7437.

sections.title: Avoiding a Delay in NomCom Setup
sections.content:
RFC 3777 required the NomCom chair to publish open positions and solicit volunteers, with at least 30 days for people to volunteer. This made the chair the only person who could start that process. Delays in naming the chair therefore delayed the committee's organization.

The RFC describes how this affected the 2008-2009 cycle: the chair was named less than 30 days before the second IETF meeting, so the committee could not conduct its interviews there.
sections.plainLanguage: The volunteer search had to wait for the chair to be appointed. If that appointment came late, the committee lost time to organize and meet.

sections.title: Starting the Volunteer Call Early
sections.content:
Four weeks after the first IETF meeting each year, the Internet Society President either names an Incoming NomCom Chair or directs the IETF Executive Director to issue the open-position announcement and volunteer solicitation on the future chair's behalf. The Executive Director collects responses and gives the volunteer names to the chair when appointed.

The solicitation may begin early, but the NomCom process cannot proceed to completion without an Incoming NomCom Chair. The Incoming or Outgoing Chair may also ask the Secretariat to perform clerical tasks that do not require chair judgment, with appropriate notice to the community.
sections.plainLanguage: If the chair has not been named by the stated point in the year, the Executive Director can start collecting volunteers. The appointed chair receives the responses and leads the committee's work.

sections.title: Scope and Status
sections.content: This memo updates RFC 3777 to allow only the position announcement and volunteer solicitation to start before a chair is named. It does not authorize the process to finish without a chair. RFC 5633 is a Best Current Practice and was later obsoleted by RFC 7437.
sections.plainLanguage: The change starts volunteer recruitment earlier, but the chair still leads the NomCom process. RFC 7437 later replaced this Best Current Practice.
